name: p2-ip-only-opentitan-rv-timer-tlul
description: One OpenTitan Earlgrey rv_timer target model behind the real beat_to_tlul register kernel, no CPU and no DMA. Every case line states the A-channel handshake (opcode/address/mask/data) the request was accepted on and the D-channel response (data/error) the transfer completed on, both sampled from the target's own taps. Expectations are the RTL's own register facts: INTR_STATE0 is rw1c and INTR_TEST0 pulses it, CTRL bit 0 is the timer-active bit, CFG0 resets to step=1/prescale=0 (0x00010000), and writing a compare register clears INTR_STATE0 through mtimecmp_update.

transactions.note: INTR_STATE0 after reset: no interrupt is latched
INTR_TEST0 bit 0 pulses the timer interrupt through prim_intr_hw
the pulsed interrupt is latched in INTR_STATE0
rw1c: writing the latched bit back clears it
CFG0 reset value: step=1 (bits 23:16) with prescale=0 (bits 11:0)

TIMER_V_LOWER0 while the timer is active: mtime advances on every tick step=1, so this word is recorded as the observed count (the first run of this batch declared 0x00000000 here and the device answered 0x00000007 - a real, undeclared advance, kept in runs/p2-ip-only-20261103/tlul-declared-mismatch)
the active timer ticks every cycle with prescale 0 and advances mtime by step=1
TIMER_V_LOWER0 after the wait: the device really advanced, the word is recorded without pinning it to a cycle-exact value
COMPARE_LOWER0_0 = 5; writing a compare register clears INTR_STATE0 through mtimecmp_update
the compare register returns the word that was written
disable the timer so the declared sequence ends from a known state
